en: When buying a television, monitor or other electronic device, consumers often focus on price and features. However, energy efficiency is equally important. Energy labels help consumers compare products and choose devices that use less electricity while providing the same service.
Choosing efficient products reduces electricity bills and contributes to protecting the environment.
The European Union uses a standard energy label system ranging from Class A (most efficient) to Class G (least efficient).
The label also provides information about annual energy consumption. Efficient devices require less electricity to perform the same task, reducing both operating costs and carbon emissions.
A more efficient television may cost slightly more when purchased, but it often saves money throughout its lifetime through lower electricity consumption.

Even an 'A' rated monitor can waste energy if the brightness is at 100% all the time. Lowering brightness to a comfortable 60% can **reduce** power consumption by nearly **20%** without hurting your eyes!
